title: play
description: Play is voluntary, intrinsically motivated activity pursued for its own sake — broader than games, becoming a game when it acquires structure. An instance describes an episode of play. Not itself a game: a game is play plus agreed structure (see ../../../services/gaming-services-section/schemas/glossary/terms/game.schema.json).

voluntary.description: The participant chose to enter; withdraw voluntariness and the activity is no longer play (Suits 1978, Huizinga 1938).

intrinsicallyMotivated.description: Pursued for its own sake; when external reward or compulsion carries the activity, the relation between participant and activity has changed.

structured.description: Whether the play has acquired agreed rules, objectives, and constraints. Structured play is gaming; a structured episode is described by the game schema.

boundedness.description: Huizinga's boundary: play proceeds within its own limits of time and place (the magic circle).

arena.description: Where the play is bounded — a board, a table, a field, a virtual world.

duration.description: The episode's own time: a match, a session, an afternoon.
